display.title: Episode 140: Reward for Kindness (Month of Elul)
display.summary_short: A girl who gave away apples from her tree discovers a hidden treasure when a storm blows the tree down; plus the Alter Rebbe's parable of the King in the field for Elul.
display.summary_long: Back from summer vacation, Uncle Yossi explains that just as rest and good food strengthen the body, davening, Torah study and daily tzedakah strengthen the soul for the new year. After the Hakochainik march and a sponsor message, a third-grade class from a Brooklyn girls' school leads the Shema. Story time begins with the greatness of tzedakah, which brings Moshiach closer, then tells of Sarah, a poor man's daughter who gave her pennies to beggars and the apples of her backyard tree to hungry families, always teaching them to thank Hashem. When a storm uproots the tree, her father reminds her that whatever Hashem does is good, and in the hole left by the roots they find a chest of treasure. Uncle Yossi then explains the month of Elul: on Rosh Hashanah our deeds are weighed, and teshuvah, tefillah and tzedakah tip the scale. He shares the Alter Rebbe's parable of the King who goes out to the field to greet his people just as they are. The show ends with a new drawing contest, the Shofar Gadol contest, with free copies of the Moshiach Times.
display.lesson: Give tzedakah with a full heart and trust that whatever Hashem does is good; in Elul the King is in the field, so come close through teshuvah, tefillah and tzedakah.

date.note: Talks about 'now, in the month of Elul' and a contest running until Rosh Hashanah; follows episode 139 (Rosh Chodesh Elul, 28 Aug 1984), so the next Tuesday.
